tagline.text: Immaculate Conception cathedral that has stood beside Roxas City's plaza for over 300 years

location.label: Location
location.text: Downtown Roxas City, Capiz, on Arsobispo Street across from the city plaza

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱100~500 (cathedral visit plus local transport and snacks)

children.text: Roxas City Cathedral began as a parish church founded by Augustinian missionaries in 1707 and is now the seat of the Archdiocese of Capiz. Close to the city plaza and the Panay River, it is a good starting point for exploring downtown on foot.

The cathedral's formal name is the Immaculate Conception Metropolitan Cathedral, and locals simply call it Roxas Cathedral. It stands in the heart of Roxas City, the capital of Capiz in northern Panay, in the historic center where the city plaza and the Capiz Provincial Capitol sit together. With the Panay River and the Capiz Bridge nearby, standing in the plaza and looking at the church facade makes it easy to see where this city began.

According to records, the parish was founded by Augustinian missionaries in 1707. Some sources also say an earlier church was destroyed by a typhoon on January 4, 1698, so the dates differ slightly depending on the source. The church was then rebuilt in 1728–1732, damaged by an earthquake in 1787, and rebuilt again in 1870–1885. Wikipedia states that the current structure dates from 1827, so this point also varies by source. A restoration and reconstruction followed in 1954. The repeated collapse and rebuilding of the church mirrors the typhoons and earthquakes this region has endured.

When the Diocese of Capiz was created on January 27, 1951, this parish church became its cathedral. The city was renamed from Capiz to Roxas on April 11 of the same year, yet the diocese kept the name Capiz. On January 17, 1976 the diocese was raised to an archdiocese, so today this is the central church of the Archdiocese of Capiz. Archbishop Jose Advincula, created a cardinal on November 28, 2020, received his red biretta and ring at this cathedral on June 18, 2021, and Archbishop Victor Bendico was installed here on May 3, 2023. On December 8, 2023, the cathedral's image of the Immaculate Conception was canonically crowned.

The exterior is described as Baroque, and the main entrance on the facade is a simple semicircular arch. Some visitors note that it is plainly decorated compared with other Catholic buildings of its era. If you expect an ornate European cathedral it may feel modest, but that is also why you can sense an everyday church that residents walk into as part of their daily lives. Google reviews often mention the detailed altar, a small garden outside, and vendors selling candles and religious items. The name Capiz comes from the capiz shell (capis) that was once abundant in the area. Capiz windows, with thin translucent shell set into the window frames, were used in old houses and convents across the Philippines. Even if you are only visiting the cathedral, you will keep running into shell-shaped monuments and shell crafts around Roxas, so thinking about the roots of the local name makes the visit richer. A visit to the church usually takes 30 minutes to an hour, and if you add the plaza, the museum and the beach, plan on a half day to a full day.
The cathedral's patron is the Immaculate Conception. The image was crowned on December 8, 2023. It is enshrined near the altar inside, so look around quietly outside Mass times.

blocks.title: A church history of over 300 years

children.text: Since the parish was founded in

, the building has been rebuilt several times after typhoons and earthquakes: 1728–1732, the 1787 earthquake, 1870–1885, and the 1954 restoration. It is fun to look at it while thinking of the layers of time built into the structure.
The facade is Baroque and the main entrance is a semicircular arch. With little ornament, the lines and proportions stand out. The soft morning light makes for good facade photos.

On special occasions the cathedral is lit up at night and draws locals and tourists. Reviews describe colorful night lighting after the renovation, so if you plan an evening visit, check locally whether the lights will be on.

blocks.title: The plaza district as one set

children.text: The cathedral is near the city plaza, which holds the Capiz Provincial Capitol, Roxas City Hall, the Manuel Roxas monument and the Panublion Museum. Don't stop at the cathedral; seeing this whole area together makes a satisfying half day.

As the seat of the Archdiocese of Capiz, it is the center of Catholic events in the region. Around Christmas and the December 8 Feast of the Immaculate Conception, more worshippers come and the atmosphere changes.
The small garden outside and the stalls selling candles and prayer items show everyday life at a small-city Philippine church. Buying a candle from a stall and lighting it is a local way to visit.

items.title: 1–2 hour cathedral walk
items.subtitle: Inside the cathedral and around the plaza

children.text: Start by photographing the facade, then step back in the plaza to see the whole exterior. Morning sun lights the facade at this hour.
Go inside and look at the altar and the image of Mary. If Mass is underway, watch quietly from the back or come at another time.
Walk the outside garden and the stall area and light a candle.
Head to the nearby plaza to see the Manuel Roxas monument and the Panublion Museum.
Opening and Mass times differ by source, so check locally before you visit.

items.title: Half-day Roxas downtown course
items.subtitle: From the cathedral to the beach

children.text: See the cathedral and plaza first, then walk toward the capitol.
Take a tricycle to La Playa de Roxas People's Park in Baybay. It has a beach facing the Sibuyan Sea and a seafood court.
Walk the beach at sunset and have dinner at the seafood court.
A direct flight from Manila to Roxas Airport (RXS) takes about
50 minutes
. Wikipedia says Cebu Pacific, Philippine Airlines and AirAsia operate three to four flights a day. Routes and frequencies change often, so check before booking.
From the airport, take a taxi or tricycle into town. Ask about the fare locally.

items.title: From Manila by sea or bus

children.text: There are RORO ferries from the Port of Culasi to Batangas (2GO and Starlite Ferries), and a Moreta Shipping Lines vessel to Manila North Harbor. The sea trip to Manila takes about
18 hours
RORO buses to Manila (Cubao) leave from the Roxas City Integrated Terminal in Lawaan. Check locally whether they are running.

items.title: By land from Iloilo or Kalibo

children.text: Iloilo City is about
2 hours
away by land. Buses to Iloilo run from the Roxas City Integrated Terminal in Lawaan and the Eastern Terminal in Banica.
Kalibo is about
86 km
away. Buses to Aklan leave from the integrated terminal, so check the timetable locally.

The cathedral is near the central plaza, so both jeepneys and tricycles pass by. A 2011 blog said a local tricycle ride cost ₱8 per person, but that is old information, so ask the fare before you ride.
Sights around the plaza can easily be covered on foot.

The cathedral is mostly an indoor visit, so you can see it even in the rain. Walking to the plaza and the beach, however, is much more pleasant in the dry season. According to PAGASA 1991–2020 normals, Roxas has a mean daily maximum of about
, a minimum of about
, and annual rainfall of about 2,137 mm (other climate datasets give roughly 2,100–2,250 mm).

The wettest months are June to October and the driest are February and March. Around the December 8 Feast of the Immaculate Conception the cathedral is crowded, so for a quiet visit we recommend a weekday morning.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Crowded around the Feast of the Immaculate Conception (December 8) and Christmas
Hot and dry, least rain in February–March
Avoid midday and walk in the morning or evening
Rainy season, heavy rain June–October, typhoon risk
On rainy days focus on the cathedral and museum

Roxas City is known as the seafood capital of the Philippines. Oysters and milkfish farming are its signature products, and it is said to export to Taiwan, Japan and the United States. After the cathedral, we recommend a meal at the seafood court in La Playa de Roxas People's Park in the Baybay area. The seafood court building is said to be designed with inspiration from the capiz shell.

Reviews say hotels on Plaridel Street in the city center, close to the cathedral, are convenient because the public market is nearby. If you want sea views, look at the Baybay beach side, and for a more comfortable new district, Pueblo de Panay is also an option. Check rates and whether a business is open before booking.
Dress modestly, with shoulders and knees covered, because it is a church.
During Mass, refrain from taking photos or speaking loudly, and do not walk in front of the altar.
Opening hours differed by source, from 24 hours to 5 AM–8 PM, so it is safest to check by phone (+63 36 621 5995) before visiting.
The cathedral alone is a short visit, so combine the plaza, the Panublion Museum, the capitol and Baybay Beach into a half-day plan.
Reviews say Sunday morning Mass is very crowded, so visit on a weekday if you want a quiet look.
Midday heat is strong, so bring a hat and water, and carry an umbrella in the rainy season.
Check the Archdiocese of Capiz announcements for church information and event schedules.
During Mass, leave the worshippers' seats free and look around quietly from the back or sides. Groups should keep their voices low out of respect.
This is a place of worship, so entry and photography for sightseeing may be restricted during Mass and events. Check the latest announcements for opening and Mass times.
Years and building history differ between sources, so give priority to the explanation on site.
Transport and flight routes and fares change often, so check again before departure.
During typhoon season flights and ferries are often cancelled, so leave room in your schedule.
Watch for pickpockets in town and keep valuables on your person.
This is the city that holds the cathedral. With seafood and Baybay Beach, it combines well with the cathedral for a day trip. For the city overall, see
Roxas City
A museum near the city plaza. It is close to the cathedral and reachable on foot. Check opening hours locally.

blocks.title: Manuel Roxas monument and city plaza

children.text: The plaza gathers the monument to Manuel Roxas, the namesake of the city, along with city hall and the capitol.
A Baroque and Neoclassical church in Panay town, Capiz, named a National Landmark in 1997 and home to the large bell Dakong Linganay. Its hours are listed as 8 AM–4 PM; check the distance on a map.

blocks.title: Pueblo de Panay and the Sacred Heart of Jesus Church

children.text: A planned township within Roxas City that has the Sacred Heart of Jesus Church. Hours are listed as 8 AM–4 PM.
